text:
sam: heads-up, enterprise customer hitting repeated 413s when uploading large embedding batches via streaming NDJSON. They say it's intermittent but mostly after ~30s into the upload.

erica: thanks — which endpoint, model, and client? any error body from our side?

sam: /v1/embeddings, model=text-embedding-3-large, they stream NDJSON lines with ~20k vectors total. curl shows 413 with empty HTML-ish body. No JSON error we can parse.

jordan: 413 normally = request body too large or proxy limit. Are they using Transfer-Encoding: chunked or setting Content-Length?

sam: they use chunked streaming from their side (node fetch, no content-length).

morgan: infra-bot flagged a few 413s from our edge (nginx) earlier today — default client_max_body_size was bumped for a canary pool but not for their region. infra-bot: I just raised client_max_body_size to 50m on the problematic layer and restarted.

erica: good catch. Two quick things to triage: 1) ask customer to retry with small chunk sizes and include a final Content-Length if possible; 2) verify whether the 413 includes our internal header X-Proxy-Reason so we can tell if it came from edge vs app.

sam: asked customer to try 5MB chunk windows. also asked for raw request/response (curl -v).

jordan: also watch out for NDJSON framing: each line must be a valid JSON with the vector. If a chunk boundary splits a UTF-8 multibyte char it can cause parse failures on our ingestion when we reassemble — but that usually yields 400, not 413.

morgan: timeline update: after config change, infra logs show fewer 413s from that region. still seeing some failures tied to a single customer IP range — looks like a WAF rule kicking in on large bursts. I'm whitelisting their CIDR for the test window.

erica: if they can't set Content-Length, prefer smaller line counts per chunk. Recommend: max ~500 vectors per NDJSON chunk or keep payload < 5MB, whichever is hit first. Also recommend inserting a short pause (200-500ms) between chunk POSTs to avoid burst throttling.

sam: customer tried smaller chunks and saw successful uploads for a while, but then started hitting dimension mismatch errors: "expected dimension 1536, got 768" in the ingestion logs.

jordan: dimension mismatch indicates model mismatch. Confirm they aren't mixing embeddings from two different model runs (e.g., text-embedding-3-small vs -large). Are they sending a metadata field that indicates model name?

sam: they weren't tagging lines. They were parallelizing two workers: one calls text-embedding-3-large, the other text-embedding-3-small into the same collection. The DB enforces a fixed vector dimension per index, so smaller vectors fail.

merica: (typo) erica: actionable: make sure collection/index is created with the correct dimension ahead of ingestion, and don't mix models. For hotfix, they can create a new index with 768 dims and route the small-model traffic there, or re-run with large model.

morgan: also note: when uploading large batches we recommend the following pattern:
```
# pseudo curl streaming pattern
# 1) chunk locally into files or buffers of <= 5MB
# 2) for each chunk:
#    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch \
#      -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
#      -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \
#      --data-binary @chunk.ndjson
#    wait 200ms between requests
```

morgan: alternative: upload the large file to their S3 and call our async/ingest endpoint with the object URL. That avoids edge body size limits and is better for multi-GB payloads.

erica: logging + repro checklist for support: 1) full curl -v showing request headers (Content-Type, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding), 2) sample NDJSON line (no PII), 3) model name used, 4) count of vectors per chunk, 5) timestamps for failures, 6) any 4xx/5xx response bodies.

jordan: also check client retry/backoff. If they retry after 413 without backoff, they may cause WAF/edge rate limits. Recommend exponential backoff on 413 as well.

sam: customer provided curl output; it shows chunked transfer with no content-length and nginx returned 413 from edge. after we whitelisted CIDR and increased client_max_body_size, their streaming completed successfully when they used consistent model.

erica: nice. follow-up: create a short KB article for support that includes: typical causes (edge body limits, WAF bursts, mixing models), recommended chunk sizes (<5MB / ~500 vectors), and the S3 async pattern. I'll draft it.

morgan: I'll also open an internal infra ticket to ensure our canary config change is propagated to all regions.

sam: tagging customer success to confirm closure. cc @customer-success: they need to confirm their ingestion is green for 24h before we close.

# reactions: :thumbsup: from erica, :eyes: from jordan
